\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{দোষ} (dosh)}{দোষ (dosh)}]{\bn{দোষ} (dosh) — a fault; blame}

\label{lesson:BN-C343-dosh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a formal complaint, then the Bengali for to settle a dispute.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{দোষ}}
\textbf{\bn{দোষ}} — \emph{dosh} — \textquotedblleft{}a fault; blame\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{এটা} \bn{তোমার} \bn{দোষ} \bn{নয়।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{eṭā tomār dosh nôy.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It's not your fault.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{দোষ}} (\emph{dosh}) is Sanskrit \emph{doṣa}, a fault or defect (Monier-Williams). It belongs to the one at fault: \bn{তোমার} \bn{দোষ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dosh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dosh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṭā tomār dosh nôy.} — It's not your fault.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a formal complaint, then the Bengali for to settle a dispute, then say \emph{dosh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{দোষ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A fault; blame\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{দায়ী} (dāyī)}{দায়ী (dāyī)}]{\bn{দায়ী} (dāyī) — responsible for a fault; to blame}

\label{lesson:BN-C343-dayi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to settle a dispute, then the Bengali for blame.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{দায়ী}}
\textbf{\bn{দায়ী}} — \emph{dāyī} — \textquotedblleft{}responsible for a fault; to blame\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দুর্ঘটনার} \bn{জন্য} \bn{কে} \bn{দায়ী}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{durghôṭônār jônyô ke dāyī?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Who is to blame for the accident?
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{দায়ী}} (\emph{dāyī}) is Sanskrit \emph{dāyin}, which Monier-Williams gives as giving and also as owing or having to pay. Bengali uses it for the one who owes an answer, the one to blame; that narrower sense is not one the dictionary gives. \bn{দায়িত্ব}, a responsibility, is its abstract.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dāyī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dāyī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{durghôṭônār jônyô ke dāyī?} — Who is to blame for the accident?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to settle a dispute, then the Bengali for blame, then say \emph{dāyī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{দায়ী} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Responsible for a fault; to blame\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ক্ষতিপূরণ} (khôtipūrôn)}{ক্ষতিপূরণ (khôtipūrôn)}]{\bn{ক্ষতিপূরণ} (khôtipūrôn) — compensation}

\label{lesson:BN-C343-khotipuron}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for blame, then the Bengali for responsible for a fault.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ক্ষতিপূরণ}}
\textbf{\bn{ক্ষতিপূরণ}} — \emph{khôtipūrôn} — \textquotedblleft{}compensation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{কোম্পানি} \bn{ক্ষতিপূরণ} \bn{দিতে} \bn{রাজি} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kompāni khôtipūrôn dite rāji hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The company agreed to pay compensation.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ক্ষতিপূরণ}} (\emph{khôtipūrôn}) is Sanskrit \emph{kṣati}, loss, with \emph{pūraṇa}, filling up (Monier-Williams): filling the hole a loss has made.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khôtipūrôn}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khôtipūrôn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kompāni khôtipūrôn dite rāji hôlô.} — The company agreed to pay compensation.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for blame, then the Bengali for responsible for a fault, then say \emph{khôtipūrôn} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{জবাবদিহি} \bn{করা} (jôbābdihi kôrā)}{জবাবদিহি করা (jôbābdihi kôrā)}]{\bn{জবাবদিহি} \bn{করা} (jôbābdihi kôrā) — to answer for; to account for}

\label{lesson:BN-C343-jobabdihi-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for responsible for a fault, then the Bengali for compensation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{জবাবদিহি} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{জবাবদিহি} \bn{করা}} — \emph{jôbābdihi kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to answer for; to account for\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{মন্ত্রীকে} \bn{এই} \bn{খরচের} \bn{জন্য} \bn{জবাবদিহি} \bn{করতে} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{môntrīke ei khôrôcher jônyô jôbābdihi kôrte hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The minister will have to answer for this spending.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{সভায়} \bn{জবাবদিহি} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini sôbhāy jôbābdihi kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{জবাবদিহি} \bn{করা}} (\emph{jôbābdihi kôrā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{javāb-dihī}, the giving of an answer, built on Arabic \emph{jawāb}, an answer; with \bn{করা} it means to explain yourself to those who can hold you to account.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôbābdihi kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôbābdihi kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{môntrīke ei khôrôcher jônyô jôbābdihi kôrte hôbe.} — The minister will have to answer for this spending.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for responsible for a fault, then the Bengali for compensation, then say \emph{jôbābdihi kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{জবাবদিহি} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To answer for; to account for\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{রেহাই} \bn{দেওয়া} (rehāi deoyā)}{রেহাই দেওয়া (rehāi deoyā)}]{\bn{রেহাই} \bn{দেওয়া} (rehāi deoyā) — to let off; to spare}

\label{lesson:BN-C343-rehai-deoya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for compensation, then the Bengali for to answer for.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{রেহাই} \bn{দেওয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{রেহাই} \bn{দেওয়া}} — \emph{rehāi deoyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to let off; to spare\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বিচারক} \bn{ছেলেটাকে} \bn{রেহাই} \bn{দিলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bichārôk chheleṭāke rehāi dilen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The judge let the boy off.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{চোরকে} \bn{রেহাই} \bn{দিলেন}, \emph{tini chorke rehāi dilen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{রেহাই} \bn{দেওয়া}} (\emph{rehāi deoyā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{rihāʾī}, release, with \bn{দেওয়া}: to give someone their release from a punishment or a duty.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rehāi deoyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rehāi deoyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bichārôk chheleṭāke rehāi dilen.} — The judge let the boy off.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for compensation, then the Bengali for to answer for, then say \emph{rehāi deoyā} again
\end{itemize}

What does \bn{রেহাই} \bn{দেওয়া} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To let off; to spare\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
